topups.why: Not needed, since five better USE rows are kept. 그녀의 형제 is also ambiguous between brother and sister, while the Welsh brawd means brother.
Not needed, since five better USE rows are kept. The Korean also reads clumsily as two run-on clauses.
Bare cyfarfod with a direct object is weaker than cyfarfod â / cwrdd â in North Welsh, and five better USE rows are already kept.

originals.ko: 나는 예전에 이사하는 것에 대해 걱정하곤 했어

originals.why: Wrong sense. Here symud means moving something physically, but this course glosses it as 이사하다 (to move house), so the Korean cannot follow the gloss.
Wrong sense. Here symud means moving a car, but the gloss is 이사하다 (to move house), so the Korean has to step outside the gloss.

originals.ko: 나는 내 돈을 옮길 수 없어
originals.why: Wrong sense. Here symud means moving money, which 이사하다 (to move house) cannot express.

originals.ko: 그들은 우리가 이사할 필요가 있다고 생각해
나는 오늘 오후에 내 돈을 옮기려고 노력하고 있어
originals.why: Wrong sense. Here symud means moving money, but the gloss is 이사하다 (to move house).

originals.ko: 너는 오늘 저녁에 네 차를 옮기지 않는 게 좋겠어
originals.why: Wrong sense. Here symud means moving a car, but the gloss is 이사하다 (to move house).
'symud ar draws' with no object is unnatural on its own; ar draws needs a noun such as 'ar draws y wlad'. Out of its source context the meaning is unclear.

refill.why: Good phrase, but only 3 USE rows are needed and the three kept give more variety (angen, reported speech, negative question).
Grammatical, but only 3 are needed and this one is weaker. 할 수 있을 텐데 maps loosely to the bare conditional fyddai.
Fine, but surplus to the 3 needed.
이사할 수 있을 거라고 equally gives 'y bydd hi'n medru' (will) and 'y byddai' (would), so it has two possible answers.
Surplus to the 3 needed. Also, without a question mark the Korean reads as a statement but the Welsh is a question.
